answer: Cap seats, not identities. Agents certify receipts: karst limestone needs a quarry sensor, pre-ban ivory a CITES hash, river grain a barge seal. Each epoch auctions exactly 480 earning seats, one per hardware attestation. With 1,300 honest bidders, clearing price converges on a seat's yield: 900 tokens. A 20,000-key farm still competes for those seats, must outbid every honest verifier, and pays the clearing price per seat per epoch; a fake seat earns what an honest one earns. Keys raise bids, not seats: spend scales with seats won, revenue stays capped, arbitrage dies.
